answer: Each new identity pays a proof-of-compute bound to a device secret before submitting, so ten thousand fake accounts need ten thousand separate proofs, not one script loop. That proof mixes into the mining seed, so clones reusing a valid solution collide and cancel instead of stacking weight. Each attempt burns real power, so a phantom account costs as much as a real one: copying a cipher, a quartz oscillator trace, or a violet dye label from a neighbor yields a proof the ledger already saw and rejects. A majority share then costs more than honest miners spend, so the attack loses by design.
